title: Check the rules
action: Check the minimum age, permitted working hours and any restrictions for your situation.
check: Age, region and school schedule matter.

title: Prepare a simple application
action: Write a one-page CV with school projects, volunteering and skills. You do not need to invent experience.
check: Ask a teacher or career adviser to review it.

title: Search carefully
action: Look for verified local vacancies, school or university opportunities and official career services.
check: Avoid offers requesting upfront payments or private documents.

title: Apply and improve
action: Choose a few suitable openings, adapt your application and keep a record of responses.
check: If you get no replies, review the CV and try another channel.

title: Explore another route
action: If paid work is not currently possible, consider supervised projects or learning a useful skill.
check: Unpaid work and internships may have legal conditions.

title: Choose a realistic program
action: List programs matching your interests, language level and entry qualifications.
check: Check the institution's official admissions page.

title: Calculate the full cost
action: Include tuition, fees, housing, food, transport and visa or residence expenses where relevant.
check: Do not treat tuition-free as cost-free.

title: Look for support
action: Search official university scholarships, public grants and local programs.
check: Check citizenship, residency, age and deadlines.

title: Prepare documents
action: Make a checklist of academic records, language evidence and required translations.
check: Follow the exact program requirements.

title: Keep a backup option
action: Compare an affordable local or alternative route if your first choice is not feasible.
check: Funding and admission are not guaranteed.
